title: SBI for experimental evolution learning assessment

knowledge_questions.title: What does each evolutionary force do?
knowledge_questions.prompt: Match each biological force to its main role in the simulator.
knowledge_questions.feedback: Mutation supplies variants, selection changes their expected reproductive contribution, and finite-population sampling produces drift.

knowledge_questions.title: Build one generation
knowledge_questions.prompt: Arrange one simulator generation using the convention used in this workshop.
knowledge_questions.feedback: This workshop advances each generation as mutation, then selection, then drift; changing that convention can change a discrete-time model.

knowledge_questions.title: Now run the logic backwards
knowledge_questions.prompt: You observed an evolutionary trajectory. How can simulations help you learn what generated it?

cards.label: Parameters θ drawn from plausible values

knowledge_questions.feedback: Candidate parameters generate simulated data. SBI compares those simulations with the observation and returns uncertainty over plausible parameters.

knowledge_questions.title: Several explanations fit
knowledge_questions.prompt: Three different parameter combinations explain the measured trajectory almost equally well. What should we conclude?

choices.label: Pick the parameter set whose curve looks best.
Keep uncertainty over the plausible parameter combinations.

knowledge_questions.feedback: When several parameter combinations are consistent with the data, the posterior should preserve that uncertainty instead of forcing one answer.

knowledge_questions.title: Build rejection ABC
knowledge_questions.prompt: Put the simulation recipe in order.

cards.label: Keep parameters whose simulations are close

knowledge_questions.feedback: Rejection ABC draws from the prior, simulates, compares with the observation, and retains parameters from sufficiently close simulations.

knowledge_questions.title: Design the observation
knowledge_questions.prompt: You can afford one additional measurement. Where would you put it?
knowledge_questions.feedback: Measure where competing hypotheses predict the largest separation: here, that is the middle interval.

confidence_questions.statement: I can turn a biological hypothesis about evolution into a stochastic simulator.
I can reason from an observed trajectory to uncertainty about the evolutionary processes or parameters that generated it.

post_evaluation_questions.statement: This workshop changed how I think about connecting mechanistic models with experimental data.
I can imagine using at least one idea from this workshop in my own research.
